en: A Praise of the Lion of the Śākyas composed by Śaṅkara:
I bow to the Victorious One, the Son of the Sugata, resplendent with a shimmering canopy.
He possesses the radiance of a thousand suns and is as pure as ten million moons;
from the circles of his pores flows a most subtle luster,
and he is adorned with lotus-hands and feet marked by the sign of the thousand-spoked wheel.
I worship the Leader of the World, the destroyer of sorrow and disease, the ender of the fear of old age and calamity, the one who carries us across the ocean of existence;
whose lotus-throne is fully blossomed and whose forest of awakening is awakened.
The creator of light for the three worlds, the sole purifier of the triple universe.
Homage be to you, who took birth as a human in the pure ocean of the Śākyas like the moon in the sea of milk;
now, consisting of the nectar of sacred narrative, you shall bring delight to the world.
Blazing forth, you shall destroy the darkness of delusion consisting of the three nets.
To him who is established at the seat of enlightenment for the welfare of the world, who has conquered the host of Māra, who reclines upon a grass mat,
and who is endowed with the ultimate perfections of the well-born Śākya king;
Salutations to you, O King of Dharma, who are surrounded by the vows of awakening! || 4 ||

I worship Him who is destined for excellence, who shatters the states of worldly existence, who is the source of the majesty of perfect enlightenment, who is most auspicious, and who possesses a portion of the beautiful; He who bore the burden of enlightenment in order to break the weight of the flood of worldly becoming.
It is radiant with the light of the auspicious sun, well-cultivated, and the bringer of purity.
In the central pavilion of the Lord of Jinas, which was spread with a shimmering canopy,
adorned with a thousand kalpa-trees, and resplendent as if perfectly complete,
the All-pervading Lord sat upon a seat of kusha grass at the edge of an altar made of gold and jewels.
I always pay homage to the Śākya Sugata, the supreme Tathāgata.
Those who recite before the Victor that auspicious fivefold set of five chowries created by Hara at the three times of day,
endowed with fame and Dharma, shine forth as the seven prosperities increase.
They go with ease to Sukhāvatī, that truly blissful realm. || 7 ||
The hymn to Śrī Śākyasiṃha composed by Śaṅkara is completed.
